a:r.a:t: The Insulin Receptor Activates a Multivalent Signalling Protein Cascade
Phosphorylated Tyr residues are bound by proteins with SH2 domains, like Grb2.
SH2 domains have multiple protein binding domains and can bring two or more proteins into close proximity.

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram that illustrates the regulation of gene expression by insulin through a MAP kinase cascade. In the first stage, the insulin receptor, which is a pinkish folded structure with two blue rounded projections coming out of it, binds insulin and undergoes autophosphorylation on its carboxyl-terminal Tyr residues. There are 6 green circles with Ps in them attached to the blue rounded projections; this represents phosphorylation. There’s also a brownish oval, labeled IRS-1, with a curved arrow pointing upward to the Ps. Once IRS-1 is phosphorylated (stage 2), another curved arrow pointing downward, points to an IRS bound to 3 Ps; two on the let of IRS-1, and one to the right. The one on the right is bound to a few structures bonded to each other; the first is a grey mass labeled Grb2, the second is Sos, the third is a green circle labeled Ras, with GTP entering and GDP exiting, and the fourth structure is a blue mass labeled Raf-1 (stage 3). In stage 4, activated Ras binds and activates Raf-1. In stage 5, Raf-1 phosphorylates MEK, represented by a blue diamond, on two Ser residues, activating it. MEK phosphorylates ERK, represented by a blue oval, on a Thr and a Tyr residue, activating it. At this point, ERK moves into the nucleus and phosphorylates nuclear transcription factors such as Elk1, activating them. ERK is now bound to two Ps on the top and bottom right. Elk1, represented by an orangish, flaglike structure, is phosphorylated and joins SRF (another orangish, flaglike structure) to stimulate the transcription and translation of a set of genes needed for cell division (stage 7). A blue DNA double helix is shown underneath SRF and Elk-1, connected to P. An arrow points at a green mRNA, and a protein leaves the reaction. This last part occurs in the nucleus, whereas the previous reactions occur in the cytosol.
